title: Fix Compose Client Lib Rs Test Isolation Poisoning
description: In compose/client/lib/rs/lib.rs, the `mod tests` suite (cargo test -p compose) shows order/parallelism-dependent cascading failures. Running the full 68-test suite three separate times (parallel default threads, --test-threads=1, and again after an unrelated refactor) each time produced 16 failures but with a DIFFERENT exact set of failing test names depending on run order/parallelism. Root cause evidence: one failure explicitly panics with "thread '...' panicked at compose/client/lib/rs/lib.rs:8187:68: the_kit_snapshot_store mutex poisoned by a prior panic: PoisonError { .. }" (see Graph::the_kit_snapshot_store, a std::sync::Mutex field declared around lib.rs:8036, locked with .expect(...) at lib.rs:8113, 8187, 8297). Many GraphQL mutation-roundtrip tests (createTag/createDesign/createQuality/createType/deleteTag/rename, all using a literal `store(id: "test-store")`) also fail nondeterministically with "missing new name: []" style assertions, consistent with shared/leaked state between tests that are supposed to be isolated (each test calls crate::gql::build_schema() which spawns a fresh ParentStore, so the isolation bug is likely in a static/global registry keyed by the literal "test-store" id, or in how Graph's per-instance mutex ends up shared/reused across what should be independent test runtimes). Fix: (1) find why a panic in one test's Graph poisons state visible to unrelated tests (look for any `static`/`OnceCell`/`lazy_static` GRAPHS or session-store registry keyed by "test-store", or any test-fixture caching that reuses a Graph/ParentStore instance across tests), (2) either make the mutex poisoning non-fatal (recover instead of .expect()) or ensure full per-test isolation so one test's panic cannot affect another, and (3) re-run `cargo test -p compose` several times (both default parallel and --test-threads=1) to confirm zero cross-test failures. Do not change test-level wiring (mod quick/mod long) that already exists in this file's mod tests block — this is a correctness/isolation bug, separate from the OVERHAUL-TEST-SUITES-TO-30S-BUDGET-PER-APP ticket.
summary:
Root cause was NOT cross-test shared state — each `#[test]` already gets a fully isolated `Graph`/`ParentStore`/`Mutex` (no static registry keyed by "test-store"; that GraphQL argument is actually unused). The real bug: `Graph::the_kit_snapshot_store` and `EventBus::path_sinks` used `std::sync::Mutex::lock().expect("...poisoned by a prior panic")` at 5 call sites. Mutex poisoning is sticky — once any transient panic occurred while a lock was held, every later lock attempt for the rest of that test failed permanently, turning one hiccup into a cascade within that single test. Which test hit the trigger first varied by timing, producing the "16 failures, different set each run" symptom described.

Fix: all 5 sites (lib.rs the_kit_snapshot_store at the reseed/materialize/dispatch call sites, and EventBus::path_sinks at emit_event/subscribe_paths) now recover via `.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner())` instead of panicking or permanently erroring. Verified across 3 independent full `cargo test -p compose --lib` runs: zero "poisoned" panics in any run.

Bonus fix found while investigating: `stored_create_fixed_piece_operation` was parsing the wrong JSON shape when replaying CreateFixedPiece via the internal VCS wire format — it assumed the flat golden-fixture shape (`{designId, blueprintId, position, ...}`) but `kit_operation_step_input_json` actually emits a doubly-wrapped shape (`{"CreateFixedPiece": {"scope": {"CreateFixedPiece": {design_id, blueprint_id, ...}}, "input": {"FixedPiece": {position, ...}}}}`). This caused a 100% deterministic `designId` panic (not a race) in 4 tests. Fixed by reusing the existing `kit_scope_from_json`/`kit_input_from_json` parsers for the wrapped shape while still supporting the flat golden-fixture shape.

Deeper finding, split into a separate follow-up task (not fixed here — out of scope, large reimplementation): `wire_json_to_canonical_kit_diff` only parses the 9 scalar `CanonicalKitDiff` fields (name/version/description/icon/image/remote/homepage/license/preview) and silently drops the 8 collection-diff fields (types/designs/tags/concepts/qualities/files/folders/families), even though `canonical_kit_diff_to_wire_json` fully serializes them. This makes every collection-mutating operation (createTag/createDesign/createConcept/createQuality/createType/createFixedPiece/etc.) report success but silently no-op when the snapshot-store VCS envelope replays it to materialize TheKit's queryable kit state. Confirmed via 3 independent full test runs producing byte-for-byte identical failure sets — this is a deterministic pre-existing gap, not the order/parallelism-dependent flakiness this ticket was opened for. Flagged as a spawned follow-up task with concrete file/line pointers rather than attempted here.
